idea-plugin.name: Ktor HttpClient Reuse Companion
idea-plugin.description:
Warning icon on a Ktor HttpClient(...) constructor call built inside a regular function body -- Ktor's own documentation states plainly: "creating HttpClient is not a cheap operation, and it's better to reuse its instance in the case of multiple requests." Building one inside a regular function means a brand new client (and its own connection pool/engine) gets created on every call.

100% static text/PSI analysis -- matches the callee name by simple text, so it works whether the real Ktor client jar is on the classpath or not. Kotlin only (Ktor has no Java equivalent). Confirmed gap: JetBrains' own bundled Ktor plugin has only 2 real inspections, both on YAML config files -- neither covers this code-level construction pattern.

Stated honestly: v0.1 only flags a direct HttpClient(...) call (with or without a trailing config lambda). Never flags a call inside a constructor or a class/top-level property initializer (legitimate "create once" locations).

Free. No license nags, no telemetry, no network calls.
